native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs clearly among habitat types in the Barcelona province, following the ordering Wetlands ~ Coastal > Riparian > Urban > Croplands: the wetter, low-elevation habitats hold the largest share of ornamental-origin species among the plants they contain, and croplands the smallest. Defining prevalence as sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) over species records in plots with n.total > 0 (conditional on a plot being invaded), Wetlands (29/52 = 0.56, Wilson 95% CI 0.42-0.68), Coastal (23/43 = 0.54, CI 0.39-0.68) and Riparian (35/96 = 0.37, CI 0.28-0.46) hold the highest shares of gardening species, while Croplands is the clear minimum (20/108 = 0.19, CI 0.12-0.27) and Urban is intermediate-low (45/151 = 0.30, CI 0.23-0.38); the region-wide value is 169/481 = 0.35. The habitat effect is confirmed by a cell-means binomial GLM on cbind(n.gard, n.total - n.gard) (LR chi2 = 36.7, df = 5, p = 6.8e-07; Pearson dispersion c = 1.01, so no beta-binomial correction is needed) and by a Monte-Carlo habitat x pathway test (chi2 = 75.2 over the 10 habitats, p < 0.001) used because 57% of asymptotic cells have expected counts < 5. Wetlands and Coastal exceed Croplands by ~1.7 logits (p < 1e-4) and Urban by ~1.0-1.1 logits (p = 0.005-0.001); Wetlands and Coastal do not differ from each other (p = 0.82). Broad-leaved forests (4/4), Coniferous forests (7/8), Scrublands (2/5), Meadows (4/13) and Rock outcrops (0/1) are NOT estimable and their extreme apparent values (1.00, 0.88, 0.00) must not be read as results: each rests on 1-13 records and they were collapsed into one composite group. Adding elevation and the UTM coordinates strengthens the fit (LR chi2 = 12.3, df = 3, p = 0.006) but leaves the habitat ranking unchanged, and residual spatial autocorrelation is not significant (Moran's I = +0.06, p = 0.17), although with only 191 non-empty plots this test has limited power. Elevation enters positively as a within-habitat partial effect (+0.0033 logit per metre, p = 0.0008) yet does not explain the between-habitat ranking - Wetlands, the highest prevalence habitat, sits at only ~176 m mean elevation. A plot-level occupancy analysis over all 632 plots (success = n.gard > 0, so the 515 plots with n.gard = 0 count as failures) reproduces the two poles - Wetlands highest (0.50) and Croplands lowest (0.21) - but reverses the middle: Urban rises to 0.48 (2nd) because 83% of urban plots host at least one invader, nearly all unintentional (104/151). The two definitions therefore disagree specifically for Urban and for the collapsed rare-habitat group (0.55 conditional vs 0.04 occupancy); rank agreement across the six groups is weak and non-significant (Spearman rho = 0.26, p = 0.62, n = 6). Finally, the regional introduction pool shifted from 16.8% gardening before 1500 to 75.2% in 1985-2019, so these habitat contrasts are differences in pathway mixture within one modern snapshot, not evidence about the rate at which each habitat receives ornamental introductions.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Read invaded_niche_pathways.csv with sep='\t' (it is tab-separated despite the .csv extension) and invasion_success_pathways.csv with the default separator; verified n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo==n.total in 632/632 plots and the 'Gardening' label match between intro.pathway and n.gard. 2) Verified the taxonomic union phylo.tip.label <-> Newick tips (81<->81, zero mismatches) and that the plot table has no species column, justifying exclusion of the tree from the model. 3) Full 10-habitat descriptive panel: plots, % plots with n.total==0 (occupancy descriptive, kept outside the model), records per pathway, prevalence sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total), Wilson 95% CI and plot-level cluster bootstrap CI (20 000 resamples), explicit estimability flag for habitats with <15 records. 4) Confirmatory test: cell-means binomial GLM on cbind(n.gard, n.total-n.gard) ~ habitat over the 191 plots with n.total>0, after collapsing the 5 habitats with <15 records; overdispersion reported (Pearson c) and quasi-scaled p-values given; pairwise log-odds contrasts via t_test. 5) Monte-Carlo habitat x pathway chi-square (20 000 simulations, row totals fixed) because 57% of asymptotic cells have expected count <5. 6) Spatial sensitivity: habitat + elevation + UTM coordinates, LR/quasi-F and AIC comparison, Moran's I with k=5 nearest-neighbour weights and 4 999 permutations on Pearson residuals. 7) Sensitivity: plot-level occupancy over all 632 plots (n.gard>0 as success, 515 zeros included), plus Spearman rank agreement with the conditional prevalence. 8) Robustness of the grouping threshold (MIN_REC 10/15/20/30) and a 5-estimable-habitat-only model. 9) Mechanism context from the species table (growth.form x pathway, Mann-Whitney on invaded.niche.breadth) and temporal bias from temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv. Fixed seed 20261022; re-runs verified byte-identical.

sub_hypo.text: Conditional on a plot being invaded, gardening-origin prevalence differs among habitats, ordered Wetlands ~ Coastal > Riparian > Urban > Croplands.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in Barcelona province in one modern snapshot; 191 plots with n.total > 0. Prevalence is sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total), not the proportion of plots occupied.
sub_hypo.relations: Wetlands: 29/52 = 0.56 (Wilson 95% CI 0.42–0.68); Coastal: 23/43 = 0.54 (0.39–0.68); Riparian: 35/96 = 0.37 (0.28–0.46); Urban: 45/151 = 0.30 (0.23–0.38); Croplands: 20/108 = 0.19 (0.12–0.27). Region-wide prevalence is 169/481 = 0.35. The six-group binomial GLM habitat effect is significant (LR chi-square = 36.7, df = 5, p = 6.8e-07); Pearson dispersion is 1.01. Wetlands and Coastal exceed Croplands by approximately 1.7 logits (p < 1e-4) and Urban by approximately 1.0–1.1 logits (p = 0.005–0.001), but do not differ from one another (p = 0.82).

sub_hypo.text: Introduction-pathway composition differs among habitat types.
sub_hypo.context: All ten habitat types in the Barcelona province plot dataset; Monte-Carlo testing is used because 57% of asymptotic cells have expected counts below five.
sub_hypo.relations: The habitat-by-pathway association is significant (Monte-Carlo chi-square = 75.2, p < 0.001; 20,000 simulations with fixed row totals).

sub_hypo.text: Individual gardening-prevalence estimates for five rare habitats are not estimable and their extreme apparent proportions must not be interpreted as habitat effects.
sub_hypo.context: Barcelona province; habitats with fewer than 15 species records are collapsed into one composite group for confirmatory analysis.
sub_hypo.relations: Broad-leaved forests (4/4), Coniferous forests (7/8), Scrublands (2/5), Meadows (4/13), and Rock outcrops (0/1) have insufficient records for separate inference; apparent proportions such as 1.00, 0.88, and 0.00 are not interpretable results.

sub_hypo.text: Elevation and spatial adjustment improve model fit without changing the habitat prevalence ranking; elevation has a positive within-habitat association rather than explaining the between-habitat ordering.
sub_hypo.context: Conditional gardening prevalence in the 191 invaded Barcelona province plots, with rare habitats collapsed and adjustment for elevation and UTM coordinates.
sub_hypo.relations: Adding elevation and UTM coordinates improves fit (LR chi-square = 12.3, df = 3, p = 0.006), while the habitat ranking remains unchanged. Elevation contributes +0.0033 logit per metre within habitats (p = 0.0008), despite highest-prevalence Wetlands having a mean elevation of approximately 176 m. Residual spatial autocorrelation is not significant (Moran's I = +0.06, p = 0.17), with limited power from 191 plots.

sub_hypo.text: Plot-level gardening occupancy and conditional gardening prevalence agree on Wetlands and Croplands as the highest and lowest estimable habitats but disagree particularly for Urban and the collapsed rare-habitat group.
sub_hypo.context: Barcelona province; occupancy uses all 632 plots, defining success as n.gard > 0 and including 515 gardening-zero plots as failures; conditional prevalence uses only plots with n.total > 0.
sub_hypo.relations: Occupancy is 0.50 in Wetlands, 0.21 in Croplands, and 0.48 in Urban, elevating Urban to second place rather than its intermediate-low conditional prevalence of 0.30. In Urban, 83% of plots contain at least one invader, and unintentional introductions account for 104/151 records. The collapsed rare-habitat group has 0.55 conditional prevalence versus 0.04 occupancy. Rank agreement across six groups is weak and non-significant (Spearman rho = 0.26, p = 0.62, n = 6).

sub_hypo.text: The regional introduction pool has shifted strongly toward gardening introductions, so modern habitat contrasts describe pathway mixtures rather than habitat-specific rates of ornamental introduction.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction pathways of non-native flora in Catalonia, comparing before 1500 with 1985–2019; habitat comparisons concern a single modern Barcelona province snapshot.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening's share of the regional introduction pool increased from 16.8% before 1500 to 75.2% in 1985–2019. Differences in modern habitat-specific gardening prevalence do not establish differences in the rate at which habitats receive ornamental introductions.
